summary: The note describes Bukovina, a region that was part of Moldavia in the Middle Ages and became an administrative division of the Habsburg Monarchy, Austrian Empire and Austria-Hungary from 1774 to 1918. After World War I Romania took control of it. In 1940 the Soviet Union annexed the northern half in violation of the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact, and that northern part is now in Ukraine.
one_line: Bukovina is a historical region once part of Moldavia, later Habsburg and Romanian territory, with its northern half now in Ukraine.
key_facts: Bukovina was a region of Moldavia during the Middle Ages.
From 1774 to 1918, the territory of Bukovina was an administrative division of the Habsburg Monarchy, the Austrian Empire, and Austria-Hungary.
After World War I, Romania established its control over Bukovina.
In 1940, the northern half of Bukovina was annexed by the Soviet Union.
The 1940 Soviet annexation of northern Bukovina violated the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact.
The northern half of Bukovina currently is part of Ukraine.
